short_description: A rhyming read-aloud for ages 0–5 with your child’s name in six rhymes, a dedication and a reading pledge. Four character looks. Hardcover or softcover.
long_description:
Whose Lap Today? is a personalized picture book for ages 0–5, printed to order as a hardcover or softcover. It is a warm, rhyming read-aloud about the best seats in town, made for one child. Their name is in six of the rhymes. Dad calls them up to the armchair, and Grandma saves them a seat. A big brother gives them a turn to sing “QUACK!” At the end of the day comes a sleepy “Goodnight.”

You choose one of four looks for the story’s child, their pronouns, who the book is from, and what they call Grandma (Nana, Abuela, Gigi and more). The family in the story is the same in every copy: Dad, Grandma, who uses a wheelchair, and a big brother. The first page is a personal dedication with your own gift message (or our warm default). Every spread has a short “Lap talk” idea for grown-ups. Pause and wait, say what you see and add one word, or offer a choice. Or stop before the fun word so your child can fill it in.

At the back are 5 simple lap games with safety notes. There is a “Books before screens” family reading pledge to sign together and a keepsake page for your child’s favorite laps.

The words are in English; names with accents (Sofía, Zoë, Ñico) print correctly. Each copy is printed on demand in 8.5 x 8.5 inch full color. It makes a lasting baby-shower, first-birthday or grandparent gift.

compliance_notes: No health or medical claims: the book is a story plus parent education and claims to treat, prevent or diagnose nothing. No diagnosis or condition wording anywhere (book, keywords, listing). Not presented as written by a speech-language pathologist or clinician. Talk strategies use plain words only, with no trademarked program names. No real brands, apps or products; the only screen is a generic phone resting face-down. No research citations. Child safety: every lap game has adult supervision and a safety line; the safety box covers the small-parts rule for under-3s (toilet-paper-tube test, about 1.25 in / 3.2 cm), no balloons, no cords, car seats (never a lap in a car), safe sleep, and stopping when the child says no. Copyright page: “© 2026 AlphaPlay LLC. Play Before Pixels is a trade name of AlphaPlay LLC.”, the website (own-site edition only), “First edition 2026 · Version 1.0 · September 2026”, and “Read together, and keep books away from mouths.” No street address is printed: the old commercial mailbox is retired and the founder’s home address must never appear (legal/ENTITY.md). If a printer or EU/UK GPSR needs a postal address, use the USPS PO Box once it exists [VERIFY]. Logo from brand/logo (horizontal lockup; one-colour white on the tomato band). Customer text is HTML-escaped, length-limited and checked for printable characters; anything unusual stops before printing and goes to the weekly review. Privacy: the child’s name is used only to print; it is not added to marketing, not committed to git, and order files are deleted after delivery [VERIFY retention with counsel]. Personalized items: state the no-change-of-mind-returns policy and misprint reprints before checkout [VERIFY the printer’s policy]. The final files must be checked against the chosen printer’s current template (Lulu, Gelato or other) before upload: trim, bleed, minimum page count, cover dimensions and spine, and CMYK/PDF-X if required. CPSIA: confirm the ordinary-book exemption applies; UK/EU: GPSR responsible person before selling there [VERIFY]. Etsy edition: no URL and no QR code (customer-voice rule 2); the build switches automatically on channel "etsy". Customer text is typeset with curly quotes and apostrophes. Customer-voice rule 15: the How to use page says “Talk, sing and read in the language you know best” and that a point, a sign, a sound or a tap on a talking device counts; it also says sitting beside counts as much as sitting on a lap. The one phone in the story rests face-down (spread 1); the brother’s light in the blanket fort is drawn as a plain flashlight so it cannot be read as a phone. Age label is 0–5 everywhere (back cover, listing, mockup), matching the baby-shower positioning and the from-the-early-months lap games.

faq.a: 32 pages: title page, dedication, 12 rhyming spreads with your child’s name in six of them and a Lap talk idea on each, 5 lap games with safety notes, a family reading pledge and a keepsake page. Front and back covers carry the name.
0–5. It is a read-aloud, so you can start in the first months; the rhymes and the pointing and counting games land best from about 1 to 5.

faq.q: Does the family in the story look like mine?
faq.a: You choose the look of the story’s child. The rest of the family is the same in every copy: Dad, Grandma (who uses a wheelchair) and a big brother, plus friends at the park. You can choose what the child calls Grandma. Many families read it as “a family full of laps”, not a portrait of their own.
Not yet. The words are in English, and accented names print correctly. Choose “Abuela” for Grandma if you like. The grown-up page says: talk, sing and read in the language you know best.

faq.q: How long does it take to arrive?
faq.a: Each book is printed for you, then shipped by our printing partner. Production and shipping times are shown before checkout. For a shower or birthday, order at least 3 weeks ahead.

faq.q: Can it ship straight to the family as a gift?
faq.a: Yes. Enter their address at checkout, and the book ships straight from the printer.

faq.q: Can I see the book before it prints?
faq.a: The product page shows every page of a sample copy. The name prints exactly as typed, so check the spelling before you pay. Books go to print automatically, so a book can't be changed after checkout.
Personalized books cannot be returned for change of mind. If a copy arrives misprinted or damaged, tell us and we will make it right.

faq.q: Can I buy a copy for a whole class or group?
faq.a: Each copy is made for one child. Class, school and group orders are not available yet.
